objects.taxonomy_description: The giraffe is distinguished by its exceptionally long neck and legs, unique ossicone head structures, and characteristic coat patterns.

diagnostic_checkpoints.Neck_Length: The animal possesses an extremely elongated neck that is significantly longer than its torso.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Leg_Proportions: The forelegs are notably long and slender, contributing to a steeply sloping back profile.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Head_Structure: The head features distinct, skin-covered bony protrusions known as ossicones rather than branched antlers or hollow horns.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Coat_Pattern: The body is covered in large, irregular polygonal patches separated by lighter-colored lines.

objects.taxonomy_description: Fleet equine mammal measuring 120-150 cm at withers with distinctive black-and-white striped coat pattern. Stripes unique to each individual, extending across body, legs, and mane. Head elongated with large dark eyes and mobile ears. Neck arched with erect bristly mane. Body robust and muscular. Legs long and slender terminating in single dark hooves. Tail long with black tufted hair. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse body hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. African equine with herd behavior. Stripes serve as camouflage and fly deterrent.
